messages:

Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.example
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Initial coordination: offline bootstrap & KMS handoff

Kimberly / Dylan,

Thanks for taking this on. We're getting the isolated rack ready at ACME-North and need to confirm the exact handoff steps for the KMS key material and bootstrapping artifacts. Two asks to start:

1) A minimal, ordered checklist we can follow on the day-of (powercycle windows, USB/air-gap media verification, manifest checks).
2) The expected signed-manifest format (what the SHA covers, key id, timestamp) and who signs it on Redwood side so our security team can map trust.

We also have a third-party auditor (Anita Rao from Vendor-Sec) who will witness the validation on site and will need to confirm the chain-of-custody record. Please include the recommended verification commands and what logs to capture.

Current timeline: planned onsite transfer the morning of 2026-12-07. Can you share a concise runbook/checklist and the signing process by EOD Monday (2026-11-30)?

Thanks,
Stefan
Ops Manager — Acme Industries

---
Note: We'll be shipping sealed media. If there are any altitude/packaging constraints that impact checksums, flag them now.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>
To: Stefan Keller <ops+deploy@acme-industries.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-11-28T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial coordination: offline bootstrap & KMS handoff

Stefan — thanks, forwarding to the team and putting a short checklist together here. High level answers up front: Redwood will provide a signed manifest (SHA256) covering the exact image tar, the signature will be made by our Release Signing Key (key-id RS-RED-042), and the on-site validation commands are included below.

Attached: redwood-offline-bootstrap-checklist.xlsx (compact runbook)

Quick checklist (summary):
- Before transfer: generate manifest and sign (Redwood signs manifest; we provide .sha256 and signer metadata)
- At handoff: verify package integrity with sha256sum and compare to signed manifest; verify signature with our public key (we will provide the PEM)
- Bootstrapping: insert media, run 'redwood-validate --manifest manifest.json --signature manifest.sig'
- Post-install: collect /var/log/redwood-install.log and 'journalctl -u redwood-agent' for artifact provenance

Verification commands (sample):
- sha256sum artifact.tar.gz | awk '{print $1}' > local.sha256
- openssl dgst -sha256 -verify redwood_release_pub.pem -signature manifest.sig manifest.json
- redwood-validate --manifest manifest.json --signature manifest.sig --verbose

I'll attach a short MD with KMS handoff notes (kms-handoff-instructions.md) describing the recommended ephemeral wrapping key flow and how to record key IDs in the chain-of-custody ledger.

Tentative owners: Kimberly Park (release signing, manifest generation), Dylan Brooks (on-call for day-of coordination).

I'll get the signed manifest and the full checklist to you by Monday EOD as requested.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Trust & Deployments Manager
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0132

[Attachment: redwood-offline-bootstrap-checklist.xlsx]

Stefan / Anita — attaching the signed manifest and public key, plus the final checklist we will use during the handoff. Answers inline:

1) Manifest KID mapping: yes — manifest.json contains 'signer_kid': 'RS-RED-042' and 'kms_wrap_id': 'vault-us-west-1/wrap-7732'. We'll provide the separate mapping sheet that links KID -> vault path and timestamp.
2) Canonical manifest: redwood-validate uses a canonical JSON canonicalization (RFC8785-like internal) before computing the digest. The manifest we sign is canonicalized; the tool prints the canonical manifest and the computed SHA256 so auditors can assert equality.

Attached files:
- acme-signed-manifest.sha256  (contains: manifest.json, manifest.sig, signer metadata)
- kms-handoff-instructions.md  (detailed steps for wrapping/unwrapping ephemeral keys and ledger entries)
- redwood-offline-bootstrap-checklist.xlsx  (finalized runbook)

Day-of notes: keep the public key on read-only media, verify signature before any write operations, and capture both the terminal output of 'redwood-validate --manifest manifest.json --signature manifest.sig --verbose' and the photos of the signed manifest on the media. We'll also circulate a completed chain-of-custody PDF after the transfer.

Please confirm receipt and I'll upload the DocuSign envelope for the chain-of-custody acceptance tomorrow morning.

Best,
Kimberly Park
